case_name: Chakradharamahanthi Vekata Maikya vs Chakradharamahanthi Vekata Ramana
acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Petitioner wife seeks transfer of original petitions pending in different courts to Srikakulam, citing distance and threat to life.

legal_principles.principle: Unduly long delay in disposal of cases can lead to blatant violation of the Rule of law and adverse impact on access to justice.
legal_principles.held: A person's access to justice is a guaranteed fundamental right under the Constitution and particularly Article 21. Denial of the right undermines public confidence in the justice delivery system and incentivises people to look for shot cuts and other fora where they feel that injustice will be done quicker.
cited_cases: United Nations Development Programme, Access to Justice-Practice Note (2004)

legal_principles.principle: Access to justice is not just about improving an individual's access to courts, but also ensuring that legal and judicial outcomes are just and inequitable.
legal_principles.held: Access to justice is, therefore, much more than improving an individual's access to courts, or guaranteeing representation. It must be defined in terms of ensuring that legal and judicial outcomes are just and inequitable [see United Nations Development Programme, Access to Justice-Practice Note (2004)]
cited_cases: United Nations Development Programme, Access to Justice-Practice Note (2004)

legal_principles.principle: The right of access to an independent judiciary is vital for the Rule of law.
legal_principles.held: It is submitted that the stay of investigation or trial for significant periods runs counter to the principle of Rule of law, wherein the rights and aspirations of citizens are intertwined with expeditious conclusion of matters.
cited_cases: Brij Mohan Lal v. Union of India and Ors (2012) 6 SCC 502

legal_principles.principle: The right to expeditious and fair trial is guaranteed by Article 21 of the Constitution.
legal_principles.held: Article 21 of the Constitution takes in its sweep the right to expeditious and fair trial. Even Article 39A of the Constitution recognises the right of citizens to equal justice and free legal aid.
cited_cases: Brij Mohan Lal v. Union of India and Ors (2012) 6 SCC 502

outcome.final_order: All Transfer Civil Miscellaneous Petitions are dismissed.
